A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Uni-LoRA and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Uni-LoRA experiments on GLUE, mathematical reasoning and instruction tuning, together with projection ablations and matched-rank LoRA comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds Uni-LoRA vision evaluations and hyperparameter sensitivity results. These qualify independently of baseline scores attributed to earlier papers.

M1.justification: The single trainable vector, frozen normalized random projection, reconstruction procedure and Algorithm 1 are retained. The new empty-column resampling footnote explains how to satisfy the existing nonempty-column condition; it does not establish a changed training or inference method.

E1.justification: v2 extends the previously NLP-only evaluation to image classification on eight datasets: OxfordPets, StanfordCars, CIFAR10, DTD, EuroSAT, FGVC, RESISC45 and CIFAR100. Existing language understanding, mathematical reasoning and instruction-tuning coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds VeRA and FourierFT comparisons for both mathematical-reasoning backbones; neither participated in this comparison in v1. The new vision comparison also introduces linear probing alongside full fine-tuning and FourierFT. Existing comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds ViT-Base/Large evaluation protocols with 20 epochs, rank 4, learning-rate searches and backbone-specific batch sizes, plus sweeps over trainable dimension and rank. Existing NLP protocols remain unchanged. The new vision settings contain discrepancies, including 74,000 versus 72,000 parameters and selected head learning rates outside the stated search grid.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 and Figures 3–4 systematically examine sensitivity to trainable dimension d and rank r on RoBERTa-Large/SST-2 and Gemma-7B/GSM8K/MATH. The original projection ablations and matched-rank instruction-tuning analysis remain; the latter moves to A.4 and Table 12.

E5.justification: v1 already reports five-seed medians with ± entries but does not explicitly identify the spread statistic. v2 identifies standard deviation in its checklist and explicitly reports five-run means and standard deviations for vision. No increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Shared numerical results are retained. v2 adds vision accuracies in Table 5, including Uni-LoRA averages of 85.15 and 88.00, VeRA/FourierFT mathematical-reasoning results in Table 3, and dimension-saturation and rank-sensitivity curves in Figures 3–4. These are additional results, not improvements to earlier same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13, Theorem 1, its nonempty-column assumption, the proof that P-transpose times P equals the identity, and the complexity analysis are retained. The resampling and LoRA-XS initialization explanations introduce no new theorem or revised proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the unified-framework, one-vector parameterization, isometry, linear projection complexity and parameter-efficiency claims. The added introductory sentence restates projection properties already established in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about vision generalization, saturation with increasing d and the accuracy-efficiency balance at rank 4. It replaces the English/text-only limitation with limited evaluation on small-to-medium NLP/CV benchmarks and narrows Appendix A.2's blanket memory advantage from LoRA and VB-LoRA to VB-LoRA.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, vision hyperparameters and resource measurements in Table 11, empty-column resampling guidance and LoRA-XS's SVD initialization detail. It also corrects the main-text hardware from A6000 GPUs to A100 80GB GPUs, matching the already stated appendix hardware.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Expanded experiments compare against already cited methods without changing the claimed relationship or novelty relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 inserts vision and sensitivity subsections, acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, and locally rewrites the mathematical-reasoning discussion. The existing scientific narrative, section order and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the vision results and configuration tables, two paired-panel sensitivity figures, and additional comparator rows in Table 3. Existing Figures 1–2 are retained, while several tables are relocated and renumbered. This substantially expands the displayed evidence.

improvement.justification: The vision evaluations and d/r sensitivity studies provide useful evidence about applicability and parameter-budget choices, while fuller mathematical comparisons and code-access information improve assessability. The gain is tempered by inconsistent vision settings and overstated comparisons: Section 4.2 claims consistent superiority over FourierFT, although Table 3 reports Mistral/GSM8K scores of 68.54 for Uni-LoRA versus 68.92 for FourierFT.
